background-information.fact: Both diagnoses worded as the CDE states them (Autism Spectrum Disorder, F84.0, without accompanying intellectual impairment, with accompanying language impairment in pragmatic language; ADHD, combined presentation, F90.2), made by the evaluating psychologist (by role, not by name), without a severity level.

She lives with her mother, her brother Diego (6) and her maternal grandmother (72), who looks after the children after school while the mother works and supports the household; the father lives in another state with no regular contact.
Methylphenidate ER 18 mg every morning since March 2026, prescribed by her psychiatrist (by role, not by name).
Born at 39 weeks with no complications; early milestones on time; teachers raised concerns in kindergarten about outbursts and playing alone.
Six months of school counseling in 2024; she has never received ABA.

Fourth grade at Ejemplo Elementary School in general education with ESE support and an IEP (Autism Spectrum Disorder primary, Other Health Impairment secondary); speech-language therapy and counseling are part of the IEP.
The family interview was in English; the grandmother speaks only Spanish.
The family's priorities as the mother states them: that she stops hurting her brother, calms down without breaking things, goes to school without a fight, has a friend and showers on her own.

medical-necessity.fact: The opening names the sources by source, without dates or names (the CDE, the Vineland-3 with the mother, the BASC-3 PRQ, the parent interview, direct observation, the IEP), the diagnosis as the CDE words it without a severity level, and the deficit areas.

Vineland-3 domain scores with percentile and level: Adaptive Behavior Composite 74 (4th percentile, Moderately Low), Communication 81 (10th), Daily Living Skills 72 (3rd), Socialization 66 (1st, Low).
The lowest subdomains, including Coping (v-scale 5) and Interpersonal Relationships (v-scale 7), with what they cover.
The Maladaptive Behavior Index (v-scale 22, Clinically Significant), with Externalizing (22, Clinically Significant) and Internalizing (19, Elevated).
What the BASC-3 PRQ shows that supports the need (the mother's relational frustration and parenting confidence at risk), in words, without its T-scores.
A safety incident argued: during direct observation in the community she pulled her wrist from her mother's hand and ran across the street.

School impairment as the IEP and the mother report it (leaving the classroom 2 to 4 times a week; refusing school on 6 of 20 days in October), with no BCBA observation at school because district approval was pending.

What maintains the behaviors (mainly escape from demands; access to preferred items for aggression), written as "is maintained by", from the reported and observed antecedents and consequences, without FAST or MAS results.

What ABA will do for each deficit area, said as what the child needs to learn (the reverse of the documented deficit) and the general approach; a named procedure, parameter, program title or support appears only where her sections, standing instructions, notes or a source give it (otherwise it is a proposal).
Caregiver training for the mother and for the grandmother, who speaks only Spanish.
Why ABA is needed at home and in the community, and how it complements, without duplicating, the school's services and psychiatry.

strengths-and-weaknesses.fact: She reads on grade level, with strong decoding and vocabulary (IEP).
Her interests and memory: trains and books about trains, train and bus schedules, drawing maps, a good memory.
Affectionate with her grandmother; helps feed the family dog.
Skills she does well that the Vineland-3 shows as relative strengths (expressive communication, gross motor), described as what she does, without scores or levels.
The needs, each sourced, named by the areas Medical Necessity uses without retelling its numbers, with what the child needs to learn.
The family's involvement as a strength (her mother and her grandmother willing to take part), which will help carry out and generalize the plan.

environmental-changes.fact: The school bus route change in early September 2026 (new driver, pickup 15 minutes earlier), with school refusal starting around then.
The grandmother's trip to Colombia from mid-December 2026 to late January 2027, and the YMCA after-school program (3:00 to 6:00 p.m.) while she is away.
The session note: the YMCA program accepted Sofía from December 15, 2026 and the mother gave it the IEP accommodations, attributed as information the BCBA obtained.
The planned move to another school zone in March 2027 with a change of school, not yet told to Sofía.
How she responds to change: distress when the route home or the evening routine changes.
Supports for the changes only as the sources, her notes or her standing instructions name them; a support they do not name is marked missing.

family-caregiver-involvement.fact: The mother takes part; she is available on weekday evenings after 5:30 p.m. and on Saturday mornings.
The grandmother is willing to learn the strategies and speaks only Spanish.
The father lives in another state with no regular contact.
The caregivers' current responses that keep the behaviors going (homework dropped, the tablet given to calm her, staying home on school mornings), as what training addresses.
The mother feels exhausted and judged and has started avoiding outings.
Caregiver training by Behavioral Skills Training, in person, never by telehealth, in Spanish for the grandmother.

generalization-and-maintenance.fact: This child's settings: home, school and the community (library, park, store).
This child's people: her mother, her grandmother, her brother Diego and her teachers.
Examples from her own goals and skill deficits (requesting a break or help, accepting changes, safe street crossing, showering, joining peer play).

discharge-and-service-fading-plan.fact: Discharge criteria for each target behavior by name (physical aggression, verbal outbursts, property destruction, leaving the area and school refusal, hand biting), tied to its baseline.

Objective discharge and fading criteria: her standard criteria when her standing instructions give them, otherwise a marker where a number is not known; no other numbers invented. (Her standard criteria are pending her confirmation.)
Criteria for the replacement and acquisition skills (for example requesting a break, safe street crossing, showering).
Caregiver criteria: the mother and the grandmother carrying out the strategies.
Transition and coordination with the school and the psychiatrist under the releases the mother signed.

risk-assessment.fact: Physical aggression toward Diego and peers: the bruise on Diego's upper arm; the 1-day suspension in May 2026 after kicking a classmate.
Threats to hurt others, and the butter knife she picked up while threatening Diego (August 2026).
Running across the street during direct observation in the community (no cars at that moment), and leaving the classroom 2 to 4 times a week.
Hand biting with red marks, and the head-banging episode in September 2026 that needed urgent care (closed with skin glue).
Property destruction, including the chair she threw at school in March 2026 (the class was evacuated).
The family's current responses to a crisis as reported, in ABA terms (Diego sent to his room, breakable things moved, waiting until she is quiet; they have never called 911).

crisis-plan.fact: The times and antecedents of highest risk (after school 3:30 to 6:00 p.m., homework, bedtime, school mornings).
No early signs, since the caregivers report none: none taken from other sources or invented, and none marked missing.
The kitchen knives kept in a high cabinet since August 2026.

The dangerous behaviors with a protocol for each (physical aggression, property destruction, self-injury, leaving the area); staff follow the plan's antecedent strategies at all times (marked missing while her plan does not name them); an adult always present in the home during sessions; the RBT or caregiver calls 911 when the situation gets out of control; incidents reported as soon as possible. Steps and de-escalation she has not given are marked missing; never restraint.
No firearms in the home, per the mother.
